label: input e during copy phase (fed-back e, from 3rd output on)
explanation: Token detector for the letter e as input in the copy phase only, i.e. when the model's own fed-back output e is read back in. Never fires in the original phase or at <DEL>, and never on any other input token. Almost silent at recall_idx 1 (e fed back as the first copied token), and active rate rises with recall_idx/t. The largest activations come from an e input late in the copy, near the end of long sequences (to_go 0-1), often where another e follows. Some inactive cases are e inputs early in short sequences.

issues: Reported test scores reproduce exactly: P 0.880, R 0.992, F1 0.932, mass recall 0.997. The copy-phase-e-only baseline also matches: P 0.727, R 1.0.

The factual claims hold on dev: zero activity in the original phase, at <DEL>, and on every non-e input token. recall_idx 1 is near-silent (560 of 500k steps, 0.3% of mass). The rate rises with recall_idx and t, and mass is concentrated at to_go 0-1.
Misses (557 steps, 0.3% of mass) are almost all weak (<=0.23 relative) activations at recall_idx 1, i.e. an e that is the first original token being fed back. This is scattered noise.

False positives (8911) are graded rather than a sharp class. Precision rises as to_go falls (0.78 at to_go>=5, 0.92 at to_go<=0) and with L (0.82 for L<=5, 0.91 for L>=8). That matches the explanation. Cutting on to_go loses more recall than it gains in precision (best F1 is still the original 0.934 on dev).

A minor secondary effect the explanation does not state: when e appears more than once among the originals (in_count>=2), precision is lower (0.77, versus 0.91 when in_count==1). It covers only about 16% of activations and is not big enough to call a systematic counterexample class.

Wording quibble: 'from 3rd output on' means the steps outputting original token 2 onward, where the fed-back e is original token 1 or later. This is consistent with recall_idx>=2 but could be read ambiguously.
